summary_1line: Dhaumya describes sacred western pilgrimage sites—especially the Narmada region—linking rivers, mountains, and hermitages with myths of gods, sages, and spiritual merit.

image_candidates.scene_text: The sacred river Narmada flows westward through groves of mango and cane while gods, sages, and celestial beings descend to bathe in its waters.
Atop the green Vaidurya mountain, a lotus-filled tank shines while gods and Gandharvas gather around its banks.
King Yayati falls from heaven onto the banks of the Viswamitra river yet regains the eternal realms among gathered sages.
